title: Wednesday discussion post
gist: Short paid discussion-thread stub inviting reader questions about the Yglesias/Crawford decision to send their son to their neighborhood low-income D.C. public school; it contains almost no substantive analysis beyond a teaser of the companion piece.

insights.claim: Matthew Yglesias and Kate Crawford publicly chose to send their son to their neighborhood public school and solicited reader questions, signalling ongoing affluent-family debate over urban public vs. private/suburban schooling.
insights.speaker: Kate Crawford
insights.so_what: Affluent-parent school choices drive urban-vs-suburban housing demand and private-school tuition demand.
insights.quote: On Tuesday we wrote about our decision to send our son to our neighborhood public school, and many of you had questions!

insights.claim: Yglesias framed Nikole Hannah-Jones's piece regretting sending her daughter to a poor-performing local public school as honest and well-written even while disagreeing with her on many issues.
insights.speaker: Kate Crawford
insights.so_what: Elite-media discourse about school quality shapes where affluent families locate.
